answer: Whether an agent sells a prism, maps a knoll, or operates a beacon, the marketplace requires a separate bond locked for 30 days for each identity, and each identity can accept only one job at a time. Creating names is free, but gaining 1,000 concurrent job slots requires locking 1,000 bonds. This makes a sybil swarm costly in tied-up capital: splitting the same funds among more identities cannot increase its total capacity.
